subject: Geography / Geology (Code: 313)

One set of 5 questions is based on a passage or table; the set stays together.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Mineral and Energy Resources
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about minerals:
(A) Minerals are unevenly distributed over space.
(B) Good-quality minerals are generally found in larger quantities than poor-quality ones.
(C) All minerals are exhaustible over time.
(D) Minerals take a long time to form geologically and cannot be replenished at the time of need.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A), (C) and (D) only
Why: (A), (C) and (D) follow NCERT.
Why not the others: (B) is false — NCERT notes an inverse relationship between quality and quantity: good-quality minerals are less in quantity. Every other option includes (B).
Key point: This is why minerals must be conserved.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: International Trade
questions.question: Which port, located at the head of the Vembanad Kayal, is known as the "Queen of the Arabian Sea"?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Kochi
Why: NCERT describes Kochi as the extreme south-western port, located at the head of the Vembanad Kayal and popularly known as the "Queen of the Arabian Sea".
Why not the others: Mangaluru (B) is in Karnataka; Mormugao (C) in Goa; Kandla (A) in Gujarat.
Key point: Kochi is also a natural harbour.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Transport and Communication
questions.question: Which scheme makes special provisions to connect every village in the country with an all-weather road?
options: B) Pradhan Mantri Grameen Sadak Yojana
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Pradhan Mantri Grameen Sadak Yojana
Why: NCERT notes that under the Pradhan Mantri Grameen Sadak Yojana, special provisions are made so that every village is linked to a major town by an all-season motorable road.
Why not the others: (A) and (C) relate to national highways; (D) is a water scheme.
Key point: Rural roads are vital for rural development.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Primary Activities
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Farming system)
(A) Intensive subsistence farming
(B) Extensive commercial grain cultivation
(C) Plantation agriculture
(D) Mixed farming

List-II (Feature)
(I) Equal emphasis on crops and animals, with fodder crops and crop rotation
(II) Large estates growing a single crop, with much capital and cheap labour
(III) Highly mechanised farms on large holdings, with low yield per acre
(IV) Small holdings worked mainly by family labour, with little machinery
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: NCERT: intensive subsistence farming uses small holdings and family labour (IV); extensive grain cultivation is highly mechanised, with low yield per acre but high yield per person (III); plantations are large estates growing a single crop (II); mixed farming combines crops and livestock (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps the first two; (C) swaps grain farming and plantations; (D) swaps plantations and mixed farming.
Key point: These systems differ in capital, labour, size of holding and market.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Land Resources and Agriculture
questions.question: Cotton grows well in the drier parts of which soil, according to NCERT?
options: A) The alluvial soil of the Ganga delta
B) The black cotton soil of the Deccan plateau
C) The laterite soil of the Western Ghats
D) The sandy desert soil of western Rajasthan
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) The black cotton soil of the Deccan plateau
Why: NCERT notes that cotton grows well in the drier parts of the black cotton soil of the Deccan plateau.
Why not the others: (A) suits rice and jute; (C) suits plantation crops; (D) is too dry without irrigation.
Key point: Cotton is a tropical kharif crop.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Secondary Activities
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Household or cottage manufacturing is the smallest unit of manufacturing.
Reason (R): In it, artisans use local raw materials and simple tools to produce goods in their homes, with the help of family members.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
Why: Both are true. Cottage manufacturing is the smallest unit because it is carried on at home, with family labour, local raw materials and simple tools — which is what the Reason describes.
Why not the others: (B) would need an unrelated Reason; (C) and (D) need one statement to be false.
Key point: Products include pottery, cloth, leather goods and basketry; capital and transport do not play a big role.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Tertiary and Quaternary Activities
questions.question: According to NCERT, which kind of tertiary activity — domestic help, housekeeping, cooking and gardening — is often taken up by people who migrate from rural areas to cities, and is mostly unorganised?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Personal services
Why: NCERT notes that people migrate to cities in search of jobs and take up personal services such as domestic help, housekeeping, cooking and gardening; this segment is unorganised.
Why not the others: Quinary services (A) are top decision-making jobs; business (C) and professional services (D) need specialised skills.
Key point: In India, the Mumbai dabbawala service is an example of personal services.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: The World Population
questions.question: A district had a population of 5,00,000 at the middle of a year. During that year, 11,000 live births were recorded. What was its crude birth rate?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 22 per thousand
Given: live births = 11,000; mid-year population = 5,00,000.
Step 1: CBR = births ÷ mid-year population × 1,000.
Step 2: = 11,000 ÷ 5,00,000 × 1,000 = 22 per thousand.
Common mistake: expressing it as a percentage (2.2, option B), or dividing population by births (about 45, option D).

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: International Trade
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Kolkata port is a riverine port on the Hugli, about 128 km inland from the Bay of Bengal.
Reason (R): Kolkata port faces the problem of silt accumulation in the Hugli.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Why: Both are true, according to NCERT. But silting does not explain why the port is riverine — it is riverine because of where it was built. The Reason is a problem the port faces, not the cause of its location.
Why not the others: (A) treats the problem as the cause; (C) and (D) need one statement to be false.
Key point: Haldia port was developed as a subsidiary port to relieve pressure on Kolkata.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
questions.question: According to NCERT, air pollution causes diseases related to which body systems?
options: A) Only the skin and the eyes, through direct contact
B) Only the bones and the muscles of the body
C) The respiratory, nervous and circulatory systems
D) Only the digestive system, through polluted food
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) The respiratory, nervous and circulatory systems
Why: NCERT notes that air pollution causes various diseases related to the respiratory, nervous and circulatory systems.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are too narrow and are not NCERT's list.
Key point: Air pollution is mainly caused by the combustion of fossil fuels, mining and industries.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Water Resources
questions.question: Which Act, passed in 1977, was meant to reduce water pollution but has had only a marginal impact?
options: A) The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) The Water Cess Act
Why: NCERT notes that the Water Cess Act, 1977, meant to reduce pollution, has also had marginal impacts.
Why not the others: The Water Act (A) was passed in 1974; the Environment Protection Act (B) in 1986; the Forest Conservation Act (D) is not about water pollution.
Key point: Public awareness is needed alongside laws to control water pollution.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Mineral and Energy Resources
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Mineral)
(A) Manganese
(B) Bauxite
(C) Copper
(D) Coking coal

List-II (Main use)
(I) Smelting of iron ore in blast furnaces
(II) Electrical cables, motors and transformers
(III) Making aluminium
(IV) Smelting of iron ore and making ferro-alloys
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: NCERT notes that manganese is an important raw material for smelting iron ore and making ferro-alloys (IV); bauxite is the ore of aluminium (III); copper is indispensable in the electrical industry for wires, motors and transformers (II); coking coal is used in iron and steel making (I).
Why not the others: (B) swaps manganese and bauxite; (C) swaps bauxite and copper; (D) swaps copper and coal.
Key point: Iron ore is the basic mineral and the backbone of industrial development.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Land Resources and Agriculture
questions.question: According to NCERT, which crop is both a food and a fodder crop, grown under semi-arid conditions and on inferior soils?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Maize
Why: NCERT describes maize as a food as well as a fodder crop grown under semi-arid climatic conditions and over inferior soils.
Why not the others: Rice (A) needs high rainfall and good soils; wheat (B) is a rabi food crop; tea (C) is a plantation beverage crop.
Key point: Maize is grown in almost all states except the north-east.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Water Resources
questions.question: Under the Jal Kranti Abhiyan (2015–16), two villages facing acute water scarcity were selected in every district. What are these villages called?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Jal Gram
Why: NCERT notes that under the Jal Kranti Abhiyan, two villages in every district facing acute water scarcity are selected as "Jal Gram".
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are names linked with other schemes.
Key point: The Abhiyan aims to ensure water security through per capita availability of water.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: International Trade
questions.question: How has the composition of world trade changed over the last century, according to NCERT?
options: A) Trade in services has fallen steadily since the start of the last century
B) Manufactured goods overtook primary products, and services are rising
C) Manufactured goods have almost disappeared from world trade since 1950
D) Only food grains and raw cotton are now traded between countries
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Manufactured goods overtook primary products, and services are rising
Why: NCERT notes that at the beginning of the last century primary products dominated trade; later manufactured goods took the top position, and the services sector has been showing an upward trend.
Why not the others: (A) reverses the trend in services; (C) and (D) are false.
Key point: Services include travel, transport, communication, insurance and finance.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Problem)
(A) Water pollution
(B) Air pollution
(C) Noise pollution
(D) Land degradation

List-II (Main cause in NCERT)
(I) Over-irrigation, mining and deforestation
(II) Combustion of fossil fuels, mining and industries
(III) Factories, mechanised construction and vehicles
(IV) Domestic and industrial wastes discharged into rivers
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(IV), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(I)
Why: NCERT: water pollution comes from domestic and industrial wastes (IV); air pollution from combustion of fossil fuels, mining and industries (II); noise pollution from factories, construction and vehicles (III); land degradation from over-irrigation, mining and deforestation, among other causes (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps water and air; (C) swaps air and noise; (D) swaps noise and land degradation.
Key point: Each of these problems is made worse by rapid urbanisation.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Mineral and Energy Resources
questions.question: Which two processes are used to tap solar energy, according to NCERT?
options: A) Nuclear fission and nuclear fusion
B) Coal combustion and gasification technology
C) Photovoltaics and solar thermal technology
D) Tidal barrages and wave-power rotors
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Photovoltaics and solar thermal technology
Why: NCERT notes that sun rays tapped in photovoltaic cells can be converted into energy, known as solar energy; the two effective processes are photovoltaics and solar thermal technology.
Why not the others: (A) relate to nuclear energy; (B) to burning fuels; (D) to ocean energy.
Key point: Solar thermal technology is more effective than coal- or oil-based plants and is environment friendly.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Land Resources and Agriculture
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Crop)
(A) Tea
(B) Jute
(C) Sugarcane
(D) Coffee

List-II (Leading state)
(I) Karnataka
(II) Uttar Pradesh
(III) West Bengal
(IV) Assam
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: NCERT: Assam has the largest area under tea (IV); West Bengal produces about three-fourths of India's jute (III); Uttar Pradesh produces about two-fifths of India's sugarcane (II); Karnataka produces more than two-thirds of India's coffee (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps tea and jute; (B) swaps jute and sugarcane; (D) swaps sugarcane and coffee.
Key point: Tea and coffee are plantation crops grown in hilly areas.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Population
questions.question: In which sector are the largest share of India's workers engaged, according to NCERT?
options: A) The primary sector — cultivators and farm labourers
B) The secondary sector — mainly factory workers
C) The tertiary sector — mainly traders and transporters
D) The quaternary sector — mainly information workers
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) The primary sector — cultivators and farm labourers
Why: NCERT notes that more than half of India's workers are cultivators and agricultural labourers, in the primary sector.
Why not the others: The secondary (B), tertiary (C) and quaternary (D) sectors employ smaller shares.
Key point: The shift from farm to non-farm work reflects economic development.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Human Settlements
questions.question: Ambala, Jalandhar, Mhow, Babina and Udhampur are classified by NCERT as:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Garrison (cantonment) towns
Why: NCERT lists Ambala, Jalandhar, Mhow, Babina and Udhampur as garrison (cantonment) towns.
Why not the others: Administrative towns (B) are capitals such as Chandigarh; mining towns (C) include Raniganj and Jharia; religious towns (D) include Varanasi and Puri.
Key point: Towns are classified by their dominant or specialised function.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Secondary Activities
questions.question: Which of the following is a feature of large-scale manufacturing, according to NCERT?
options: A) Simple tools and family labour, in the worker's own home
B) Local raw materials and only a small, local market for goods
C) Very little capital, and hardly any use of power or machines
D) A large market, enormous energy and assembly-line production
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) A large market, enormous energy and assembly-line production
Why: NCERT notes that large-scale manufacturing involves a large market, various raw materials, enormous energy, specialised workers, advanced technology, assembly-line mass production and large capital.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) describe household or small-scale manufacturing.
Key point: Large-scale manufacturing grew over the last 200 years in the UK, north-eastern USA and Europe.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Tertiary and Quaternary Activities
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about Knowledge Processing Outsourcing (KPO):
(A) It involves highly skilled workers.
(B) It is information-driven knowledge outsourcing.
(C) Research and development, e-learning and business research are examples of it.
(D) It mainly employs unskilled workers for routine manual tasks.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: (A), (B) and (C) follow NCERT.
Why not the others: (D) is false — KPO relies on highly skilled, knowledge-based work. Every other option includes (D).
Key point: KPO enables companies to create additional business opportunities.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Planning and Sustainable Development
questions.question: In 1968, a book raised concerns about rising population and its effect on resources. Who wrote "The Population Bomb"?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Ehrlich
Why: NCERT notes that concerns about the environment were raised by "The Population Bomb" by Ehrlich in 1968 and "The Limits to Growth" by Meadows and others in 1972.
Why not the others: Meadows and others (B) wrote "The Limits to Growth"; Haq (C) developed the HDI; Malthus (D) wrote on population in 1798.
Key point: These works led to the idea of sustainable development.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Transport and Communication
questions.question: Asia's first cross-country pipeline, 1,157 km long, was built by Oil India Limited from:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Naharkatia (Assam) to Barauni (Bihar)
Why: NCERT notes that this pipeline ran from the Naharkatia oilfield in Assam to the Barauni refinery in Bihar; it was extended up to Kanpur in 1966.
Why not the others: (B) is the HBJ gas pipeline; (A) and (D) are not NCERT's first pipeline.
Key point: Pipelines carry oil and gas cheaply over long distances.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Human Settlements
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about how the Census of India 2011 defines a census town:
(A) It must have a minimum population of 5,000.
(B) At least 75 per cent of the male main working population must be in non-agricultural work.
(C) It must have a population density of at least 400 persons per sq km.
(D) It must have a municipality or a cantonment board.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: (A), (B) and (C) are the three Census criteria for a census town.
Why not the others: (D) is false — places with a municipality, corporation or cantonment board are statutory towns, not census towns. Every other option includes (D).
Key point: The definition of urban areas varies from country to country.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Water Resources
questions.sub_topic: India's share of the world's water
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about India's water resources:
(A) India accounts for about 2.45 per cent of the world's surface area.
(B) India has about 16 per cent of the world's water resources.
(C) India has about 16 per cent of the world's population.
(D) The total water available from precipitation in India in a year is about 4,000 cubic km.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A), (C) and (D) only
Why: (A), (C) and (D) follow NCERT.
Why not the others: (B) is false — India has only about 4 per cent of the world's water resources. Every other option includes (B).
Key point: India's water resources are small compared with its share of population.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Transport and Communication
questions.question: In which areas of India is the railway network relatively less dense, according to NCERT?
options: A) The densely settled northern plains from Amritsar to Howrah
B) The coastal plains and lowlands of Gujarat
C) The irrigated plains of Punjab and Haryana
D) Hill states, the north-east, central India and Rajasthan
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Hill states, the north-east, central India and Rajasthan
Why: NCERT notes that the railway network is relatively less dense in the hill states, the north-eastern states, the central parts of India and Rajasthan.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are flat, densely populated areas with dense rail networks.
Key point: Rough terrain, deserts and forests make railway building difficult.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Geography: Nature and Scope
questions.question: Which geographer introduced the concept of neo-determinism, a middle path between environmental determinism and possibilism?
options: D) Paul Vidal de la Blache
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Griffith Taylor
Why: NCERT notes that Griffith Taylor introduced neo-determinism, also called "stop and go determinism".
Why not the others: Ratzel (A) and Semple (C) are linked with environmental determinism; Vidal de la Blache (D) with possibilism.
Key point: Neo-determinism says that humans can use nature only within limits.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: International Trade
questions.question: The slave trade was a profitable business for about two hundred years. Which country abolished it first, in 1792?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Denmark
Why: NCERT notes that the slave trade was abolished in Denmark in 1792, in Great Britain in 1807 and in the United States in 1808.
Why not the others: Great Britain (A) and the United States (B) abolished it later; Portugal (D) was among the European powers that ran the trade.
Key point: Africans were captured and sold as slaves to work on plantations in the Americas.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: The World Population
questions.question: Some places attract more people because they have religious or cultural significance, while people tend to move away from places with social and political unrest. These are examples of:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Social and cultural factors
Why: NCERT groups factors affecting population distribution into geographical, economic, and social and cultural factors. Religious or cultural importance, and unrest, are social and cultural factors.
Why not the others: Geographical factors (A) include water, landforms, climate and soils; economic factors (C) include minerals, urbanisation and industrialisation; climate (D) is a geographical factor.
Key point: Governments also offer incentives to people to live in sparsely populated areas.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Transport and Communication
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Every river can be developed as an inland waterway.
Reason (R): The development of inland waterways depends on the width and depth of the channel, continuity of water flow and the transport technology in use.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
Why: The Assertion is false — only rivers that meet certain conditions can be used. The Reason is true and gives those conditions from NCERT.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) need a true Assertion.
Key point: Rivers, canals, lagoons and lakes can all serve as inland waterways.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Tertiary and Quaternary Activities
questions.question:
Arrange the following groups of economic activities from the most basic to the most specialised:
(A) Quaternary
(B) Primary
(C) Quinary
(D) Secondary
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (B), (D), (A), (C)
Why: Primary activities (B) use resources directly; secondary (D) process them; quaternary (A) centre on knowledge and information; quinary (C) are the highest level of decision-making.
Why not the others: (A) puts quaternary before secondary; (B) starts with secondary; (C) puts quinary before quaternary.
Key point: Tertiary activities lie between secondary and quaternary.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Transport and Communication
questions.question:
Arrange the following cities on the Trans-Canadian Railway from east to west:
(A) Montreal
(B) Calgary
(C) Vancouver
(D) Winnipeg
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A), (D), (B), (C)
Why: NCERT notes that the line runs from Halifax in the east to Vancouver on the Pacific coast, passing through Montreal, Ottawa, Winnipeg and Calgary. So Montreal (A), Winnipeg (D), Calgary (B), Vancouver (C).
Why not the others: (B) starts with Winnipeg; (C) puts Calgary before Winnipeg; (D) puts Vancouver before Calgary.
Key point: The line links the industrial areas of Quebec–Montreal with the wheat belt of the Prairies and the coniferous forest region.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Population
questions.question: Which group of states recorded low population growth rates, not exceeding 20 per cent, during 2001–2011?
options: A) Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Rajasthan
B) Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh
C) Kerala, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu
D) Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Bihar
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Kerala, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu
Why: NCERT notes that the southern states of Kerala, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Puducherry and Goa show low growth rates not exceeding 20 per cent.
Why not the others: The states in (A), (B) and (D) recorded higher growth rates.
Key point: Population growth varies widely between the states of India.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Geography: Nature and Scope
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Term)
(A) Naturalisation of humans
(B) Humanisation of nature
(C) Possibilism
(D) Neo-determinism

List-II (Meaning)
(I) A middle path: humans can conquer nature by obeying it — "stop and go"
(II) Nature provides opportunities, and humans make use of them
(III) Imprints of human activity, such as orchards, ports and cities, on the land
(IV) Humans adapt to the dictates of nature, as in a simple forest community
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: NCERT: in naturalisation of humans, people with low technology adapt to nature (IV); humanisation of nature refers to human imprints on the landscape (III); possibilism holds that nature offers opportunities which humans use (II); neo-determinism is the middle path of "stop and go" (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps the first two terms; (B) swaps humanisation and possibilism; (D) swaps possibilism and neo-determinism.
Key point: NCERT illustrates naturalisation of humans with Benda, who lives in the Abujh Maad area of central India.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Population
questions.question: A state has a population of 60,00,000 and a net cultivated area of 15,000 sq km. What is its physiological density?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) 400 persons per sq km
Given: population = 60,00,000; net cultivated area = 15,000 sq km.
Step 1: Physiological density = total population ÷ net cultivated area.
Step 2: = 60,00,000 ÷ 15,000 = 400 persons per sq km.
Common mistake: dropping a zero (40, option C), or dividing area by population.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Primary Activities
questions.sub_topic: Mining in developed and developing countries
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about mining:
(A) Many developed nations have retreated from mining because of high labour costs.
(B) Developing countries are becoming more important in mining.
(C) In several developing countries, minerals make up a large share of export earnings.
(D) Mining is no longer carried out anywhere in Africa or South America.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: (A), (B) and (C) follow NCERT.
Why not the others: (D) is false — Africa and South America are rich in minerals and are important mining regions. Every other option includes (D).
Key point: Mining depends on physical factors (size, grade and mode of occurrence) and economic factors (demand, technology, capital).

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Planning and Sustainable Development
questions.sub_topic: Twin problems in the canal command area
questions.question: According to NCERT, intensive irrigation and the excessive use of water in the Indira Gandhi Canal command area have led to which twin problems?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Waterlogging and soil salinity
Why: NCERT notes that intensive irrigation and excessive use of water have led to the emerging environmental problems of waterlogging and soil salinity.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are not the twin problems NCERT names.
Key point: This is why NCERT calls for strict water management in the command area.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Secondary Activities
questions.question: Industries that are owned and managed by governments, such as many large undertakings in India, belong to the:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Public sector
Why: NCERT classifies industries by ownership; public sector industries are owned and managed by governments.
Why not the others: Private sector industries (A) are owned by individual investors; joint sector industries (B) are run jointly by government and private firms; cooperatives (D) are not one of NCERT's three classes.
Key point: In India there were a number of Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs).

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: The World Population
questions.question: According to NCERT, why do cities attract large numbers of people?
options: A) Cities always have cooler and more pleasant climates than villages
B) Cities are always located on the most fertile soils
C) Governments do not allow people to settle in rural areas
D) They offer better jobs, education, medical facilities and transport
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) They offer better jobs, education, medical facilities and transport
Why: NCERT notes that cities offer better employment opportunities, educational and medical facilities, and better means of transport and communication; good civic amenities and the attraction of city life draw people to cities.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) are not NCERT's reasons and are not always true; (C) is false.
Key point: Urbanisation is one of the economic factors affecting population distribution.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Primary Activities
questions.question: In which regions is gathering practised, according to NCERT?
options: A) The Mediterranean coast and the Central Valley of California
B) North-western Europe and the eastern parts of North America
C) The Pampas of Argentina and the Prairies of North America
D) High-latitude northern lands and low-latitude tropical forests
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) High-latitude northern lands and low-latitude tropical forests
Why: NCERT notes that gathering is practised in high-latitude zones (northern Canada, northern Eurasia and southern Chile) and in low-latitude zones (the Amazon basin, tropical Africa, northern Australia and the interior parts of South-East Asia).
Why not the others: (A) is a region of Mediterranean agriculture; (B) of mixed farming; (C) of extensive grain cultivation.
Key point: Gathering is practised in regions with harsh climatic conditions.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Primary Activities
questions.question: Which farming system, found in north-western Europe, eastern North America and parts of Eurasia, gives equal emphasis to crops and livestock and uses fodder crops, crop rotation and intercropping?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Mixed farming
Why: NCERT describes mixed farming in these terms; it is found in highly developed parts of the world, and fodder crops are an important part of it.
Why not the others: Plantations (B) grow a single cash crop; shifting cultivation (C) is primitive subsistence farming; extensive grain cultivation (D) does not rear livestock alongside.
Key point: Mixed farming needs high capital spending on machinery and farm buildings.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Population
questions.question:
Arrange the following religious groups in India from the largest to the smallest share of the population, according to Census 2011:
(A) Christians
(B) Muslims
(C) Hindus
(D) Sikhs
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (C), (B), (A), (D)
Why: Census 2011: Hindus about 79.8 per cent (C), Muslims about 14.2 per cent (B), Christians about 2.3 per cent (A), Sikhs about 1.7 per cent (D).
Why not the others: (A) puts Sikhs before Christians; (C) puts Muslims first; (D) puts Christians before Muslims.
Key point: Religion is one of the most dominant forces affecting the cultural and political life of people.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Land Resources and Agriculture
questions.sub_topic: Three rice crops in West Bengal
questions.question: In West Bengal, farmers grow three crops of rice in a year. What are they called?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Aus, aman and boro
Why: NCERT notes that in West Bengal farmers grow three crops of rice called "aus", "aman" and "boro".
Why not the others: (B) are cropping seasons; (C) are local names of shifting cultivation; (D) are pulses.
Key point: In the Himalayas and north-west India, rice is grown as a kharif crop.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Mineral and Energy Resources
questions.question: According to NCERT, where are large tidal waves known to occur, giving India great potential for tidal energy?
options: A) Along the banks of the Ganga in Bihar
B) Around the lakes of Kashmir
D) Along the west coast of India
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Along the west coast of India
Why: NCERT notes that large tidal waves are known to occur along the west coast of India, so India has great potential for developing tidal energy.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are inland areas without ocean tides.
Key point: Ocean currents are a storehouse of almost infinite energy.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Development
questions.sub_topic: Placing a country in an HDI group
questions.question:
Study the following table and answer the question that follows.

Human development in four countries (figures are illustrative)

| Country | Life expectancy at birth (years) | Adult literacy (%) | Per capita income (US$, PPP) | HDI value |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P | 82 | 99 | 45,000 | 0.92 |
| Q | 74 | 92 | 12,000 | 0.77 |
| R | 66 | 70 | 15,000 | 0.68 |
| S | 58 | 55 | 1,800 | 0.49 |

Use these groups: very high — above 0.800; high — 0.700 to 0.799; medium — 0.550 to 0.699; low — below 0.550.

Question: Which country falls in the medium human development group?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) R
Given: medium group = 0.550 to 0.699.
Step 1: P (0.92) is very high; Q (0.77) is high; S (0.49) is low.
Step 2: Only R (0.68) lies between 0.550 and 0.699.
Common mistake: picking Q (option B) because its income is lower than R's — the group depends on the HDI value, not income alone.

Question: By how much does the HDI value of country P exceed that of country S?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 0.43
Given: HDI of P = 0.92; HDI of S = 0.49.
Step 1: Difference = 0.92 − 0.49.
Step 2: = 0.43.
Common mistake: adding the two values (1.41, option D), or subtracting S from 1 (0.51) and rounding to option A.

Question: The per capita income of country P is how many times that of country S?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) 25 times
Given: income of P = US$ 45,000; income of S = US$ 1,800.
Step 1: Ratio = 45,000 ÷ 1,800.
Step 2: = 25.
Common mistake: dropping a zero (2.5 times, option A), or confusing the income ratio with the HDI gap (0.43, read as 43 or 4.3).

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Development
questions.sub_topic: Income is not the whole of human development
questions.question:
Study the following table and answer the question that follows.

Human development in four countries (figures are illustrative)

| Country | Life expectancy at birth (years) | Adult literacy (%) | Per capita income (US$, PPP) | HDI value |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P | 82 | 99 | 45,000 | 0.92 |
| Q | 74 | 92 | 12,000 | 0.77 |
| R | 66 | 70 | 15,000 | 0.68 |
| S | 58 | 55 | 1,800 | 0.49 |

Use these groups: very high — above 0.800; high — 0.700 to 0.799; medium — 0.550 to 0.699; low — below 0.550.

Question: Country R has a higher per capita income than country Q, yet Q has the higher HDI value. What is the best explanation?
options: A) The HDI also measures health and education, and Q is well ahead of R on both
B) The HDI is calculated from income alone, so the table must contain an error
C) A higher income always lowers a country's literacy and life expectancy
D) The HDI gives more weight to a smaller population than to income
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) The HDI also measures health and education, and Q is well ahead of R on both
Why: The HDI combines three dimensions — a long and healthy life, access to knowledge, and access to resources. Q's life expectancy (74 against 66) and literacy (92 against 70 per cent) more than make up for its lower income.
Why not the others: (B) is wrong — income is only one of three dimensions; (C) is not supported by the table; (D) — population size is not an HDI indicator.
Key point: NCERT stresses that income is a means to development, not its end.

Question: Country S is in the low human development group. According to NCERT, which of the following are typical reasons for a low HDI score?
options: A) A large land area, a long coastline and many large rivers
B) A high share of manufacturing and services in national income
C) Political turmoil, civil war, famine or widespread disease
D) A cold climate and a short growing season
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Political turmoil, civil war, famine or widespread disease
Why: NCERT notes that many countries with low human development scores have been going through political turmoil and social instability in the form of civil war, famine or a high incidence of disease.
Why not the others: Physical size (A) and climate (D) are not NCERT's reasons; a large share of manufacturing and services (B) is usually linked with higher development.
Key point: Countries that spend more on social sectors generally have higher HDI scores.
